citation: Beyond the classroom: how parents view motivation as a key to self-directed learning in township schools (Siziba, Geduld & Du Toit-Brits, Frontiers in Education, 2025)

claims.text: Connectivity is treated as essential infrastructure because a friendly learning environment requires reliable access to information.
evaluative_rules: Judge a learning environment by its connectivity and access to information.

claims.text: Parents own the motivating role — prompting, monitoring schoolwork, and authoring their own target-and-reward incentive schemes — because children are seen to rely on external regulation to initiate effort.
evaluative_rules: Set the targets and attach the rewards yourself when a child lacks initiative — motivating is the parent's own job, done through parent-authored standards and incentives.
objections: Is my child motivated enough to use this without constant shouting?

claims.text: Fatigue and logistical constraints limit capacity because work and household duties exhaust the energy required for homework assistance.
evaluative_rules: Acknowledge that fatigue and logistics limit the capacity to assist with schoolwork.
objections: Will this require more time than I have after work and chores?

claims.text: Parental support is supplementary because determined children initiate their own study and only request help when stuck.
evaluative_rules: Provide targeted assistance only when requested, respecting the child's existing agency.
objections: Am I just topping on what they already do, or doing it for them?

claims.text: Motivational interventions are viewed as insufficient because structural unemployment and developmental rebellion override individual encouragement.
evaluative_rules: Recognize that external structural barriers may outweigh individual motivational efforts.
objections: Does this account for the lack of jobs even for graduates?

confidence: Single-district qualitative interviews with 10 township parents (Sebokeng West, Gauteng); educated parents overrepresented in articulate responses; mechanisms durable, magnitudes and prevalence unknown
